answer.read: Edelstahl-Service Donautal opened at €6.05, no clause, 30 d payment, 12 months (offer:70710-0). It is still open and has not yet given ground. Its strongest need is an AS-14404 pass-through once its hedge expires in March 2027 (Z, doc:20260706-70710-M1). It also wants planning security before the year-end notice window and to keep its main-source quota (Z ctr:4600070710#3.1). It values volume and longer commitments (Z). It leans on the twelve-month index rises it quoted [S]. However, the alloy surcharge fell over the last quarter (a1) and PPI-C2431 also eased (a4). Our recent orders were at €5.45 (a5), which matches the estimate of its full cost.
answer.message: Thank you for your offer. We value the partnership and are prepared to give you planning security with a longer commitment, at a price basis that reflects where your input costs actually stand today. Recent alloy surcharge and producer price movements point downward, and our current order history sits well below your quote. We look forward to your response on the attached terms.
answer.reason: o9 has the same lowest C as E0 (€952,980) because our horizon is two years, so a 24-month term gives us everything a 36-month term would. It is also less binding and better fits the supplier's wish for a secure basis through the notice window. The 12-month options and the clause options cost us about €83k more. The clause also gives away the protection the supplier most needs, which we should hold back as a later concession in exchange for price. I cite a1, a4 and a5 because these recent downward moves and our order history weaken its cost argument. I leave out the delivery and forecast points to keep the message focused.
